title: SSE buf.find loop uses to_string() clone for each block; buf.drain is fine but block clone avoids borrow
description: In run_sse: let block = buf[..pos].to_string(); buf.drain(..pos+2); — the to_string() clone before drain is forced by the borrow checker (drain needs &mut buf). This is the idiomatic way to handle this split in Rust. Not elegance-negative, just worth noting: the comment explaining why clone-before-drain is needed is absent, which will confuse future readers who try to 'optimize away the clone' and hit a borrow error.
